comments.value:
To rehash my idea from the contents of another feedback post:

I think there should be an AI Disclosure Checklist (Effectively, a "Nutrition Label"), that developers can check when they upload or update a world.

It'd have categories like:

- Thumbnail

- Artwork (Non-model assets; GFX, photos, etc.)

- Textures (Model assets)

- Models

- Sound

- Code

- Layout (Object positioning & world structure)

- Assets (Non-image assets; UI assets; etc.)

This would allow developers to disclose which elements involved AI at a basic level.

The UI for user in VRChat would then have an "AI Facts" section in world listings that would list each checked item.

The idea is that developers who only use AI to *assist* in world creation are not totally penalized by flagging their entire world as AI, and so developers can be encouraged to be forthcoming with what parts they did use AI for.

details:
I know I can't be the only one who has seen an uptick in AI generated content used in recent worlds on VRChat, specifically when it comes to pictures, art, or textures. I feel that this will only get worse because there is now Discord servers and websites that also let you generate 3D content using AI. 

I've already seen so many worlds use AI art and hang it on walls which is often disturbing and uncanny looking. I recommend adding a way for world creators to disclose this by ticking a box when uploading a world that lets players know if the game contains AI or not for full transparency.
title: Disclose AI Generated Content in Worlds
